name: Jeroboam the son of Joash
charge: Doing evil in the sight of the Lord; not departing from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat
summary: Jeroboam the son of Joash reigned forty-one years over Israel and restored the coast from Hamath to the sea of the plain, as the Lord had spoken by Jonah the prophet. The Lord saw that Israel’s affliction was bitter and saved them by his hand, yet Jeroboam did evil and departed not from Jeroboam’s sins.
offense: Jeroboam the son of Joash began to reign in the fifteenth year of Amaziah and reigned forty-one years in Samaria. He did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin (2 Kings 14:23–24). The longest reign of any northern king carried no reform with it. He restored the coast of Israel from the entering of Hamath unto the sea of the plain, according to the word of the Lord spoken by the hand of his servant Jonah the son of Amittai (2 Kings 14:25). The restoration was accomplished through him, yet it was the Lord’s doing, because the Lord saw the affliction of Israel, that it was very bitter: there was not any shut up, nor any left, nor any helper for Israel (2 Kings 14:26).
judgment: The Lord said not that he would blot out the name of Israel from under heaven but saved them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash (2 Kings 14:27). The deliverance was not because of Jeroboam’s righteousness but because of the Lord’s mercy toward His afflicted people. Jeroboam slept with his fathers, and Zechariah his son reigned in his stead (2 Kings 14:29). The prosperity of his reign did not secure his house: Zechariah was slain after six months, fulfilling the word that Jehu’s house would sit on the throne unto the fourth generation (2 Kings 15:12). The kingdom was saved through an evil king and then taken from his descendants according to a limit already spoken.

verses.text: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel began to reign in Samaria, and reigned forty and one years.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.

He restored the coast of Israel from the entering of Hamath unto the sea of the plain, according to the word of the Lord God of Israel, which he spake by the hand of his servant Jonah, the son of Amittai, the prophet, which was of Gath–hepher.
For the Lord saw the affliction of Israel, that it was very bitter: for there was not any shut up, nor any left, nor any helper for Israel.
And the Lord said not that he would blot out the name of Israel from under heaven: but he saved them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash.

Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might, how he warred, and how he recovered Damascus, and Hamath, which belonged to Judah, for Israel, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Jeroboam slept with his fathers, even with the kings of Israel; and Zachariah his son reigned in his stead.

text.text: Then Amaziah the priest of Beth–el sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words.
For thus Amos saith, Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land.

entries.commentary: Amaziah the son of Joash began to reign over Judah at twenty-five and reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. He did that which was right in the sight of the Most High, yet not like David his father, meaning he did not serve with a perfect heart. When the kingdom was confirmed, he slew the servants who had killed his father, but did not slay their children, according to the law of Moses that every man is put to death for his own sin. -
Amaziah slew ten thousand of Edom in the valley of salt and took Selah by war, calling its name Joktheel unto this day.

Amaziah sent to Jehoash king of Israel to face one another in battle, and Jehoash answered with the parable of the thistle and the cedar, warning him to stay home lest he fall. Amaziah would not hear, so the two faced one another at Bethshemesh, and Judah was put to the worse before Israel and fled. Jehoash broke down the wall of Jerusalem, took the gold, silver, and vessels from the house of the Most High and the king's house, took hostages, and returned to Samaria.

Jehoash slept with his fathers and Jeroboam his son reigned in his place. Amaziah lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash, and a conspiracy was made against him in Jerusalem so that he fled to Lachish and was slain there. The people took Azariah, sixteen years old, and made him king in the place of his father Amaziah.

Jeroboam the son of Joash, Jeroboam II, began to reign over Israel and reigned forty-one years, doing evil and not departing from the sins of the first Jeroboam. He restored the coast of Israel according to the word spoken by Jonah the son of Amittai, for the Most High saw the bitter affliction of Israel and would not blot out their name. The Most High saved them by the hand of Jeroboam, who recovered Damascus and Hamath, and when he slept with his fathers Zechariah his son reigned in his place. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)
